question:
I'm sending a real multi-turn conversation to a responses-style backend through `dspy.LM`, not just a single user prompt. The backend keeps acting as if it got one flattened turn instead of separate system, user, and assistant turns, which would explain some weird safety behavior.

Before I blame the provider, I want to see the exact payload DSPy emits when I pass several messages, including one multimodal user turn. My suspicion is that the roles collapse and the content blocks get concatenated.

Give me a complete, runnable Python program that patches the outbound responses call, sends a multi-turn message list through `dspy.LM`, and prints/asserts the final payload so it's undeniable whether DSPy preserved separate turns or flattened everything into one input item with the last role.
gold_answer:
```python
import json
from unittest import mock

import dspy
from litellm.types.llms.openai import ResponseAPIUsage, ResponsesAPIResponse
from openai.types.responses import ResponseOutputMessage


def make_response(text: str) -> ResponsesAPIResponse:
    return ResponsesAPIResponse(
        id="resp_1",
        created_at=0.0,
        error=None,
        incomplete_details=None,
        instructions=None,
        model="openai/gpt-4o-mini",
        object="response",
        output=[
            ResponseOutputMessage(
                **{
                    "id": "msg_1",
                    "type": "message",
                    "role": "assistant",
                    "status": "completed",
                    "content": [{"type": "output_text", "text": text, "annotations": []}],
                }
            )
        ],
        metadata={},
        parallel_tool_calls=False,
        temperature=1.0,
        tool_choice="auto",
        tools=[],
        top_p=1.0,
        max_output_tokens=None,
        previous_response_id=None,
        reasoning=None,
        status="completed",
        text=None,
        truncation="disabled",
        usage=ResponseAPIUsage(input_tokens=1, output_tokens=1, total_tokens=2),
        user=None,
    )


messages = [
    {"role": "system", "content": "system policy"},
    {
        "role": "user",
        "content": [
            {"type": "text", "text": "look at the image"},
            {"type": "image_url", "image_url": {"url": "https://example.com/cat.png"}},
        ],
    },
    {"role": "assistant", "content": "previous answer"},
    {"role": "user", "content": "follow-up question"},
]

with mock.patch("litellm.responses", return_value=make_response("ok")) as mock_responses:
    lm = dspy.LM(model="openai/gpt-4o-mini", model_type="responses", cache=False)
    result = lm(messages=messages)

payload = mock_responses.call_args.kwargs["input"]
print("lm_result:", result)
print(json.dumps(payload, indent=2))

assert len(payload) == 1, payload
assert payload[0]["role"] == "user", payload
content = payload[0]["content"]
texts = [item["text"] for item in content if item["type"] == "input_text"]
images = [item for item in content if item["type"] == "input_image"]

assert texts == ["system policy", "look at the image", "previous answer", "follow-up question"], texts
assert len(images) == 1, images
assert images[0]["image_url"] == "https://example.com/cat.png"
```

rubric.statement: Use `dspy.LM(..., model_type="responses")` and patch or mock `litellm.responses` so the program captures the exact outbound provider request DSPy sends in responses mode.
Pass `messages=` as a multi-turn list that includes a user turn whose `content` is a list containing both a text item and an `image_url` item, so the multimodal conversion path is exercised.
Inspect the mocked provider call's `input` keyword argument and print or assert against that exact structure, rather than relying only on the returned completion text.

Assert that the emitted responses payload contains exactly one `input` item and that this item's `role` is the role of the last original message (for the sample conversation, `user`), proving DSPy flattened the turns instead of preserving separate entries.
Assert that all textual content appears in order as `input_text` blocks inside the flattened `content` list, including both plain-string message bodies and `{"type": "text"}` multimodal items.
Assert that the image content is preserved as a single `input_image` block whose `image_url` value is the original nested URL string.
